Thanks for the ping. TL;DR: we can issue a provisional PO and accept line‑level mapping via CSV. Details below.

Process & timelines:
- Provisional PO behavior: We issue a TEMP PO token in the format TEMP‑PTC‑###### within 24–48 hours after receipt of vendor tax info and completed vendor_setup_form.pdf. That TEMP PO is valid for 60 days; once the vendor is fully onboarded a permanent PO (PO‑#####) will be created and we remap invoices to the permanent PO.
- Spend caps: internal policy requires Finance approval for any monthly cap > $50,000. For <$50k we can set the cap via the PO metadata and operationally block invoices beyond the cap. $25,000/month is fine to set without escalation.
- Line items & mapping: We support per-line metadata (cost_center, sku_code). Use the attached po_mapping_template.csv to supply your line mappings. If ProcureTech will be sending consolidated invoices, include the mapping on each invoice line; otherwise we can attach the mapping during PO conversion.
- Corrections: If a line item needs post‑invoice correction, submit a credit memo referencing the TEMP PO and the line item id; we'll route to accounting for adjustment.

Required from ProcureTech to issue TEMP PO:
1) Completed vendor_setup_form.pdf (signed)
2) Tax ID (EIN)
3) Primary billing email and first invoice sample (PDF)

Attachments: po_mapping_template.csv (csv)

I'll take point on issuing the TEMP PO once the items above are in. Laura, please advise if we need legal sign‑off for the contract — looks like standard terms but want to confirm.

—Ben
